title: Evaluation of an earlier block
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $\ell$ be a list of bit sources, and let $T$ be a time parameter. Let $E_w(r)$ denote the Boolean block prescribed by the configuration encoding of input $w$ at index $r$. If a list of blocks agrees with $E_w(r)$ at every index $r<i$, then, for any $a<i$ and any bit position $j$, evaluating the block source that refers to block $a$, bit $j$ gives the $j$th bit of $E_w(a)$, with false used when that bit position is out of range.
hypotheses_covered: The list of blocks agrees with the configuration encoding at every index less than i
